Hey so I was trying to go to sleep last night and had one of those recurring ideas pop up into my head that I thought was pretty interesting so I wanted to share it. I highly doubt this would be possible with the way BZ code is made. Based on what I heard it seems like it would require completely rewriting much of the games code, but I wanted to share it anyway.

The idea is a BZII realism mod.

Basically it would include things like this:

- hovering vehicles would be significantly faster and responsive to thrust than they are in VSR as we currently have the technology IRL to do these things, evident in the US missile defense programs Multiple Kill Vehicle.
- projectiles would move significantly faster and ammo would not regenerate.
- different parts of vehicles could be damaged and need to be repaired. I.e. if you get shot in the thruster your movement would be impaired, if your weapons get shot you would run into malfunctions when using them.
- ammo capacity would be greatly reduced, especially with regards to missiles and rockets.
- missiles/rockets would deal tremendous damage compared to what they do right now, i.e. one shad would pretty much instakill a scout vehicle, similar to how modern explosives would behave.
- walking vehicles would have a greater advantage in scaling uneven terrain just like they do IRL, especially compared to tracked/wheeled vehicles.
- color schemes would be different, camo patterns and solid colors would be available for different environments
- crashing into buildings/rocks/hard surfaces would require immediate repairs. Learn to drive.
- if your cockpit got shot, the pilot would die just like with sniper. Let's be real for a second, if an assault blast shot bored a fucking hole through an isdf scouts cockpit the pilot would be disintegrated.
- mines would NOT be droppable from 500m in the air, thank you very much.

Battlezone Combat Commander is not Fortnite, where every map is a gold mine and a bunch of people go to the contest for likes. There are only a couple dozen active people, and each additional content really enlivens the game.

I think something like this: "Who the hell said "this is mine", the main thing is that the game lives and people enjoy it." And, on the one hand, this is healthy - a small community cannot afford tough competition and a war for authorship without damaging the game itself. In this sense, the philosophy is justified and pragmatic: energy is saved for creation, and not for friction.

On the other hand, for an author who is proud of his map, this is a little offensive - your work can be reinterpreted or appropriated, and no one will blink. Here it all comes down to priorities: which goal is more important - recognition of the author or the life of the game.

In Battlezone, it's almost a moral law: "the fewer people there are, the less sense there is in focusing on ego - it's more important that the game lives."

There are some handy tricks I've found through experiments which I will probably put on the tool.
Mostly using separate ODFs for different purposes when it comes to things like Scav and Cons management.

```ini
[Plan4] // Try to maintain at least 3 Scavs on the field at a time for better income.
planType = "BuildLoop"
planPriority = 85
planCondition = "Lua"
buildType1 = "ivscavcpu"
buildCount1 = 1
LuaFunction = "BuildPoolScavengerCondition"
ContinueEvenIfFail = true

[Plan5] // Try to maintain at least 4 Scavs on the field at a time for better income.
planType = "BuildLoop"
planPriority = 80
planCondition = "Lua"
buildType1 = "ivscav"
buildCount1 = 1
LuaFunction = "BuildFieldScavengerCondition"
ContinueEvenIfFail = true

[Plan6]
planType = "BuildMinimums"
planPriority = 75
planCondition = "Lua"
buildType1 = "ivconscpu"
buildCount1 = 1
buildType2 = "ivcons" // Specifically used to upgrade and/or build Gun Towers.
buildCount2 = 1
LuaFunction = "BuildConstructorCondition"
```

In this case, I used `ivscavcpu` specifically for chasing pools, and `ivscav` for chasing scrap. It stops the AIP from tripping over itself if it doesn't have enough Scavs for tasks, doesn't build unnecessary scav spam, etc.
